LESSON: SCALE DRAWING

Grade: Grade 8
Subject: MATHEMATICS
Strand: Geometry 4.2 Coordinates and graphs (14 lessons) • Cartesian plane • Points on t
Topic 4.3: Scale Drawing
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 14

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Scale Drawing, part of Geometry 4.2 Coordinates and graphs (14 lessons) • Cartesian plane • Points on t in Grade 8 MATHEMATICS.

Key inquiry question: How do we determine scales in real life? 2. Where do we use scale drawing in real-life situations?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

A. represent length to a given scale in different situations,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Scale Drawing in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

B. convert actual length to scale length in real-life situations,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Scale Drawing in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

C. convert scale length to actual length in real-life situations,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Scale Drawing in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

D. interpret linear scales in statement form in different situations,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Scale Drawing in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

E. write linear scales in statement form in different situations,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Scale Drawing in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

F. interpret linear scales in ratio form in different situations,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Scale Drawing in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

G. write linear scales in ratio form in different situations,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Scale Drawing in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

H. convert linear scale from statement form to ratio

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Scale Drawing in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

I. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. measure and represent length of different objects from immediate environment in his/her work book,

2. discuss and practice converting scale from one form to another,

3. read, discuss and interpret given linear scales in statement form,

4. discuss and write given linear scales in statement form,

5. read, discuss and interpret given linear scales in ratio form,

6. discuss and carry out conversions of scales from one form to another,

7. make scale drawings on different learning 1.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. measure and represent length of different objects from immediate environment in his/her work book,
2. discuss and practice converting scale from one form to another,
3. read, discuss and interpret given linear scales in statement form,
4. discuss and write given linear scales in statement form,
5. read, discuss and interpret given linear scales in ratio form,
6. discuss and carry out conversions of scales from one form to another,
7. make scale drawings on different learning 1.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Scale Drawing together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Communication and Collaboration: as the learner discusses and practices converting scale from one form to another.

• Critical thinking and Problem solving: as the learner discusses and writes given linear scales in statement form.

• Digital literacy: as the learner uses ICT devices to display the maps and use the zoom functions to demonstrate scale.

Values

• Responsibility: as the learner makes scale drawings on different learning materials using appropriate scale.

• Citizenship: as the learner uses maps to demonstrate scale and locate places.
